verdict.rationale: Framer documents several first-party programmatic surfaces. The Server API covers automated publishing. The External Agent connection gives AI tools direct access to the canvas, components, CMS and project context. The Plugin API can modify anything on the Canvas. Together these cover much of the UI's scope, but no document claims or demonstrates full API/UI parity, and the probe found no public OpenAPI spec. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or reference showing every UI action is exposed via API, API coverage of publish settings, branching/merge, staging, password protection and version rollback, a published OpenAPI/endpoint reference, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Server API Connect your product and automate publishing with the Framer API.
the native Framer External Agent connection gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex... direct access to your canvas, components, CMS, and project context
Once connected, the agent can read and write CMS collections, including creating, updating, and deleting items.
They enable you to perform various actions such as inserting images, layers and code components or modifying anything on the Canvas.
